newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - June 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- SING TAO -- The U.S. and British governments will send officials to attend the swearing-in of the provisional legislature. In a move they said was not a stamp of approval for the unelected body, they will send diplomats, not ministers.

-- MING PAO -- An international management consultancy said average salary levels in Hong Kong ranked second highest in the world, beaten only by the United States, and salaries in Shanghai were fast gaining ground.

-- Many local hotels have cut room rates by 50 percent after experts said they had set prices too high. While tourists wanted to come and witness the handover, they did not want to pay crazy prices. The overall occupancy rate has reached 90 percent.

-- WEN WEI PO -- China announced new rules to regulate travel by its nationals abroad, requiring them to travel in groups of at least three. About 67 travel agents were authorised to handle overseas tours.

-- TA KUNG PAO - The governor of Shandong said state enterprises were still the dominant factor in the province's economic development. He said most state enterprises had abandoned the old fashioned management style under the planned economy and had started to rely more on themselves.

-- APPLE DAILY -- Beijing feared some people in Taiwan might "create trouble" during Hong Kong's handover. But sources said Beijing no longer treated the Democrats as enemies and appreciated their sensible attitudes, and was more concerned about triads and gangsters.
-- TIN TIN DAILY -- Because of lack of finances, a bronze statue of the late Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping in Shenzhen cannot be completed before the handover as expected.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Cable and Wireless would not be required to further sell down its 54.5 percent stake in Hongkong Telecom until after China Telecom (Hong Kong) was floated on the stock exchange, according to well placed sources.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Two Hong Kong companies with mainland links -- Rex International Development and Cheong Yee Ltd -- will be forcibly shut dow tomorrow over government suspicions they were involved in arms deals.
